title: Integration dependency ledger
description: Every integration, add-on or bridge the reference setups rely on, with the repos that use it and a disposition. The ledger exists because a dependency list that only records what is used cannot tell a later phase what it is allowed to build on: `require` means the product may assume it, `replace` means there is something better and it is named, and `avoid` means it is abandoned upstream and the successor is named. A disposition with no successor would be an opinion.

name.description: The integration, add-on or bridge as Home Assistant spells it.

repos.description: The repos that use it. The count is what decides `require`: three or more repos using an integration is the corroboration that makes it safe to assume.

disposition.description: Required on every entry. An entry with no disposition records a dependency without saying whether the product may take it, which is the question the ledger exists to answer.

replacement.description: The successor. Required on a `replace` or `avoid` entry, and null on a `require` one -- a dependency the product may simply use has nothing it is being replaced by, and a non-null value there would be a second, contradictory answer to the same question.
